note: Cloud accounting software, San Jose (as in the Battery and Sutter Hill books); acq. by The Sage Group, 2017. Wikipedia: the Series A was raised in 2000 from HWVP, and the rounds from 2001 to 2014 were led by Battery, BVP, Sigma and Emergence; the firm's own listing dates its investment 2008-03-31, eight years after the Series A, so the entry is a later round (Growth) and the Seed band read off the $3M Form D of 2010 is disputed. Not a Seed entry, so no graduation.

Mac security software, founded in Paris in 1997 and run from Seattle and Austin (Wikipedia); acq. by Kape Technologies, 2018. The firm's own listing dates its investment 2007-06-06 and names no round; a Google News query on 2026-10-01 returned no funding report.

Virtualized IT management layer, Newton, Massachusetts, with development in Israel (NoCamels). NoCamels (2013-01-21) reports the $8.6M Series A without naming its investors; model: Bessemer led it, which matches the firm's own date of 2012-11-29, so the pre-filled 2014 date (the Form D of the next round) is replaced. The last trace is a small Form D in late 2018 and the firm's list dropped the company after 2019, so its present state is not established.

Self-optimizing network software for mobile operators, Ra'anana, Israel; acq. by Cisco, 2013. The firm's own post of 2026-06-01 says it backed Intucell 'as a sole investor' and the listing dates the investment 2011-01-12; neither names the round, so the stage is undetermined.

funding_rounds.round: only venture round, Bessemer the sole investor

note: Hospitalist physician group, North Hollywood (Los Angeles); IPO in January 2008, acq. by TeamHealth, 2015. The firm's own list gives 1997 and 1998 and names no round; the 2007 S-1 shows Bessemer Venture Partners IV and Bessec Ventures IV holding preferred stock without saying which series they bought first.

Detect-and-avoid systems for drones, San Francisco (the company's 2020 release; as in the YC book); acq. by uAvionix, 2023 (the firm's listing). The Series B release of 2020-12-15 names Bessemer a follow-on investor; model: Bessemer led the $8M Series A announced in January 2018, which matches the firm's own date of 2017-12-22.

iSIGHT Partners, cyber threat intelligence, Dallas; acq. by FireEye, 2016. Model: Bessemer made the $30M Series C investment announced in January 2015 (the firm's own year reads 2014); two Google News queries on 2026-10-01 returned no report to cite.

Antisense drug developer, Carlsbad, renamed Ionis Pharmaceuticals in 2015 (NASDAQ: IONS, market cap $7.41B on 2026-10-01, StockAnalysis, the same band as the pre-filled figure). The firm's own list: Chris Gabrieli 'invested in and served as Chairman of Isis', and the 2001 proxy calls him a founder and a director from January 1989; no round is named, so the stage is undetermined. This row and the base row ionis-pharmaceuticals are one company.

AI content platform for marketing teams, Austin (as in the Coatue, Insight and IVP books). The firm's own post of 2022-10-18: Bessemer's growth practice joins the $125 million Series A at a $1.5 billion valuation; the mark is older than 24 months, and the 2023 report of a lower internal valuation was not a priced event. The former-unicorn record on the row and the Northzone and Sequoia rows are another Jasper (Jasper Technologies, bought by Cisco in 2016).

Mobile stores that bring local vendors' goods to neighborhoods. Pulse 2.0 (2023-10-11): a $2.9M seed led by Bessemer Venture Partners; it places the company in the San Francisco Bay Area without naming the city. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Risk, investigations and compliance advisory firm founded by Jules Kroll as K2 Intelligence, New York (Wikipedia). The firm's own year is 2010 and it names no round; a Google News query on 2026-10-01 returned no funding report.

Chip-to-chip interconnect technology, Lausanne (FinSMEs). The firm's own listing dates its investment 2016-06-15; FinSMEs (2020-11-17) has Bessemer leading the existing investors in the Series C, but no source read names the 2016 round. Value check 2026-10-01: the $225M round of March 2026 valued Kandou AI at $400M (The Next Web), below $1B.
Risk-based vulnerability management, San Francisco; acq. by Cisco, 2021. PYMNTS (2018-03-30): $25 million in Series C funding, Bessemer Venture Partners leading; the firm's own date is 2018-03-09.

Keynote Systems, internet performance measurement, San Mateo. The firm's own listing: in 1997 BVP's David Cowan led the Series A round in Keynote; IPO in 1999 (NASDAQ: KEYN), then acq. by Thoma Bravo, 2013, and merged with Dynatrace in 2015.

Home swapping network (livekindred.com), San Francisco (as in the a16z and NEA books). TechCrunch (2022-04-21): a $7.75M seed led by Andreessen Horowitz with Bessemer Venture Partners participating. Graduated: the $15M Series A of April 2023 led by NEA, Bessemer among the existing backers (FinSMEs). Value check 2026-10-01: the $125M Series B and C announced in February 2026 carried no disclosed valuation (Tech Funding News), so below_1b under Rule A. The First Round and GV rows named Kindred are another company (Kindred AI, robotics).

note: Travel experiences booking platform based in Hong Kong (Wikipedia; as in the TCV book), not mainland China as the pre-filled name match read. Wikipedia: the US$210 million Series E+ of December 2023 was led by Bessemer Venture Partners, the firm's partnered year. Klook filed for a US listing in November 2025 and delayed it into 2026 (Business Times, 2025-12-02); it had not listed by 2026-10-01, so the private status stands.

Adaptive learning technology, New York; Wiley bought its assets in 2019. Wikipedia: after a $2.5M first round from Accel and others, the $6 million round of April 2009 was led by Bessemer Venture Partners with returning investors, which matches the firm's own date of 2009-03-30; a second round, so Growth, and the Series A band read off the 2010 Form D is disputed.
Credit rating agency (KBRA), New York. The firm's own listing: acq. by Wharf Street Ratings, 2015 (its exit year); the agency continues to operate under later owners.

Targeted protein degradation biotech, Watertown, Massachusetts; NASDAQ: KYMR since 2020 (market cap $9.5B on 2026-10-01, StockAnalysis, the same band as the pre-filled figure). The S-1: the Bessemer funds bought $10.0M of the Series B convertible preferred stock sold in November 2018, when Andrew Hedin joined the board, and its related-party tables name them in no earlier financing (the 2017 seed and Series A units went to Atlas Venture), so the entry is Growth.

Feature management platform, Oakland (as in the Insight book). The firm's own post of 2019-03-13: Bessemer leads the $44 million Series C, its partnered year. Mark: the $200M round of August 2021 at $3 billion (Forbes headline), older than 24 months; no later priced round found (Google News, 2026-10-01).

Networking semiconductor developer, Caesarea, Israel; acq. by Cisco, 2016 (Haaretz headline: Cisco acquires Israel's Leaba Semiconductor for $320 million). The firm's own listing dates its investment 2014-08-12, the founding year, and names no round; the company announced no funding before the sale.

Procurement and cost management software for Japanese enterprises (leaner.co.jp, the company's own Japanese site), Tokyo. The firm's own year is 2024 and it names no round; two Google News queries on 2026-10-01 returned no funding report in English.
